To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the most reasonable metabolic system of glycerol metabolism in K. pneumoniae is the system that glycerol and1,3-PDs cross the cell membrane by both active transport and passive diffusions.
the most probable metabolic network for glycerol metabolism by K. pneumoniae is a network in which glycerol and PD are transported into cells by active transport and diffusion, respectively.
both glycerols and 1, 3-PDs are transported by active transport and diffusion across the cell membrane.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel approach to the inference of biological transport mechanisms by means of robustness analysis of dynamical systems.
a new aspect of the glycerol bioconversion process, i.e., the transport mechanisms of substrates and products across the cell membrane.
the modeling of biochemical networks of glycerol metabolism and the inference of the transport mechanisms of two key compounds across the cell membrane.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

K. pneumoniae has a metabolic network of glycerol metabolism consisting of glycerol transport by active transport and diffusion, glycerol metabolism and 1, 3-PD transport by active transport, diffusion and efflux.
the glycerol and the 1,3-pd transport mechanisms across the cell membrane of K. pneumoniae can be inferred to be the active transport and passive transport, respectively.

the transport mechanisms of these two substrates across the cell membrane can be inferred as follows: glycerol enters the cytosol by active transport, while 1,3PD leaves the cytosol via active transport or diffusion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the robustness analysis can be used to identify the most reasonable metabolic networks among all possible ones, which can be further used for the design and optimization of biological systems.

the robustness of a metabolic network is a crucial criterion in inferring the transport mechanism for glycerol and other metabolic compounds across the cell membrane and that the most possible transport mechanism for glycolysis and 1,2-propanediol is active transport and passive transport, respectively.
the most reasonable metabolic model is the one with the highest robustness, and the robustness of a metabolic network is determined by the robustness of its dynamical system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transport mechanisms can be inferred by the robustness of the metabolic network.
the biological robustness is an important criterion for evaluating the validity of a metabolic model and the transport mechanism of glycerol across the cell membrane.
the biological robustness is an effective indicator for inferring the transport mechanisms of biochemical substances across the cell membrane.
